title: Status Register
body:
[[Trace Bit]]
[[Supervisor State]]
[[Interrupt Mask]]

Two different things share this name, and both matter in this course:

**On the [[Motorola 68000]].** A 16-bit register holding the processor's mode, not data.
The system half holds the [[Trace Bit]] (single-step), the [[Supervisor State]] bit
(privileged or not), and the three-bit [[Interrupt Mask]] (current [[IPL]]); the user half
holds the [[Status Bits]] (condition codes) that branches test. It is pushed automatically
when an interrupt is taken and restored by `rte`, which is why an [[ISRs|ISR]] cannot
disturb the interrupted program's flags.

**On an [[I-O Interface]].** The read-only register the device reports through: is there a
byte waiting, is the transmitter empty, did a parity or framing error occur, did an
[[overrun]] happen. This is the register [[Polling]] spins on. Alongside the
[[Data Register]] and the [[Control Register]].
